body.gap: No located TWSF result computes the full five-component variance shares or the direct and recursive Gaussian maximum limits on a persistent common-origin sequence.

body.proof_tex:
Set \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\).  To prove nonemptiness, take all five block dimensions equal to \(n\), use singleton menus and pairwise disjoint fitting, response, selection, and terminal cells at one common forecast origin, set every donor and target loading and every relevant conditional mean time factor equal to one, and put independent \(N(0,\sigma_n^2)\) errors on all primitive cells, with \(c_\sigma\le\sigma_n\le C_\sigma\).  Every population design is then an \(n\)-by-\(n\) all-ones matrix.  It has rank and Hankel rank one, sole nonzero singular value \(n\), and bounded entries.  Every required recovered vector is a multiple of \(\boldsymbol1_n\), so all unit, direct, and recursive recovery and transport conditions hold.  If
\(A_n=\Pi_n(\boldsymbol1_n/n)\), then
\[
 \|A_n^j\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le(1+n^{-1/2})^j
 \le\exp(H_n/\sqrt n)=O(1),\qquad 0\le j\le H_n.
 \tag{1}
\]
The variance calculation below supplies the required variance floor.  This constructs a member of \(\mathcal A_n\); since \(\mathrm{def{:}persistent\mbox{-}subclass}\) defines it by adding conditions to \(\mathcal C_n\), it also gives \(\mathcal A_n\subset\mathcal C_n\).

The Moore--Penrose inverse of \(\boldsymbol1_n\boldsymbol1_n^\top\) is
\(n^{-2}\boldsymbol1_n\boldsymbol1_n^\top\).  Hence
\[
 \beta_n=a_n=a_{n,\ell}=\frac{\boldsymbol1_n}{n},\qquad
 p_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}=\frac{\boldsymbol1_n}{n},\qquad
 q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}=\frac{\boldsymbol1_n}{n}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Put \(c_{n,\ell}=(1+1/n)^{\ell-1}\).  From
\[
 g_{n,1}=\frac{\boldsymbol1_n}{n},\qquad
 g_{n,\ell+1}=S_n^\top g_{n,\ell}
 +\frac{\boldsymbol1_n}{n}(g_{n,\ell})_n,
\]
induction gives, for \(1\le\ell\le H_n<n\),
\[
 (g_{n,\ell})_i=
 \begin{cases}
 (c_{n,\ell}-c_{n,\ell-i})/n,&i<\ell,\\
 c_{n,\ell}/n,&i\ge\ell.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{3}
\]
The same induction shows \(\boldsymbol1_n^\top g_{n,\ell}=1\).  Squaring (3) gives the exact identity
\[
 \|g_{n,\ell}\|_2^2=
 \frac{(n-\ell+1)c_{n,\ell}^2+
 \sum_{j=1}^{\ell-1}(c_{n,\ell}-c_{n,j})^2}{n^2}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Uniformly for \(\ell\le H_n=o(n)\),
\(c_{n,\ell}=1+O(H_n/n)\), so (4) yields
\[
 \|g_{n,\ell}\|_2^2=\frac1n+O\!\left(\frac{H_n}{n^2}\right).
 \tag{5}
\]

Next, \(A_n\boldsymbol1_n=\boldsymbol1_n\), and direct iteration of the last coordinate gives
\[
 e_n^\top A_n^je_n=
 \begin{cases}
 1,&j=0,\\
 n^{-1}(1+1/n)^{j-1},&1\le j<n.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{6}
\]
Differentiate \(g_{n,\ell}(x)=\{\Pi_n(x)^\ell\}^\top e_n\) in an arbitrary direction \(h\).  The product rule, (6), and \(A_n^k\boldsymbol1_n=\boldsymbol1_n\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 h^\top J_{n,\ell}^\top\boldsymbol1_n
 &=\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-1}(e_n^\top A_n^je_n)
     h^\top A_n^{\ell-1-j}\boldsymbol1_n\\
 &=\left\{1+\frac1n\sum_{j=0}^{\ell-2}(1+1/n)^j\right\}
   h^\top\boldsymbol1_n
 =c_{n,\ell}h^\top\boldsymbol1_n.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since this holds for every \(h\),
\[
 J_{n,\ell}^\top\boldsymbol1_n=c_{n,\ell}\boldsymbol1_n.
 \tag{7}
\]
Using \(\boldsymbol1_n^\top g_{n,\ell}=1\), the remaining representers are therefore
\[
 p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}=\frac{\boldsymbol1_n}{n},\qquad
 q_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}=c_{n,\ell}\frac{\boldsymbol1_n}{n}.
 \tag{8}
\]

Substitute (2) into the direct covariance formula proved in
\(\mathrm{thm{:}relative\mbox{-}gram\mbox{-}rate}\).  Its diagonal is
\[
 s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^2
 =\sigma_n^2\left\{\frac1{n^2}+\frac1n\left(1+\frac1n\right)
 +\frac1n\left(1+\frac1n\right)\right\}
 =\frac{\sigma_n^2}{n}\left(2+\frac3n\right).
 \tag{9}
\]
The lead-specific direct response term has variance \(\sigma_n^2/n\).  Consequently
\[
 \nu_{n,\ell}=\nu_{\min,n}=\nu_{\max,n}
 =\frac{1}{2+3/n}.
 \tag{10}
\]
For \(\ell\ne k\), the only omitted diagonal contribution is that independent response term, so the direct correlation is exactly
\[
 R_{\mathrm{dir},n}(\ell,k)
 =(1-\nu_n)+\nu_n\mathbf1\{\ell=k\},\qquad
 \nu_n=(2+3/n)^{-1}.
 \tag{11}
\]
Thus a version of the standardized direct score process is
\[
 X_{n,\ell}=\sqrt{1-\nu_n}\,Z_0+\sqrt{\nu_n}\,Z_\ell,
 \tag{12}
\]
where \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_{H_n}\) are independent standard normals.

Let \(M_H=\max_{\ell\le H}|Z_\ell|\).  The Gaussian union bound gives
\(\Pr(M_H>(1+\eta)\sqrt{2\log H})\to0\), while the density lower bound used in the proof of \(\mathrm{thm{:}complexity\mbox{-}frontier}\) and independence give
\(\Pr(M_H<(1-\eta)\sqrt{2\log H})\to0\).  Integration of the union-bound tail also gives uniform integrability after division by \(\sqrt{2\log H}\).  Hence
\[
 \frac{M_H}{\sqrt{2\log H}}\longrightarrow1
 \quad\text{in probability and in mean}.
 \tag{13}
\]
The deterministic inequality
\[
 \left|\max_{\ell\le H_n}|X_{n,\ell}|-\sqrt{\nu_n}M_{H_n}\right|
 \le\sqrt{1-\nu_n}|Z_0|
\]
together with \(\nu_n\to1/2\) and (13) proves
\[
 \frac{\kappa_{\mathrm{dir},n}}{\sqrt{\log H_n}}\longrightarrow1.
 \tag{14}
\]
It also proves convergence in probability of the normalized maximum to one.  Therefore every fixed \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile, divided by \(\sqrt{\log H_n}\), tends to one: for each \(\varepsilon>0\), the distribution puts probability tending to one in \([1-\varepsilon,1+\varepsilon]\), which traps its fixed interior quantile there.

For recursion put
\(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{rec},n}:=\sigma(\mathcal F_n,\widehat d_{\mathrm{rec},n})\)
and define
\[
 U_n:=n^{-1}\boldsymbol1_n^\top\delta_{\beta,n},\qquad
 V_n:=n^{-1}\boldsymbol1_n^\top\delta_{\mathrm{rec},n}.
\]
The disjoint-block assumption makes \(U_n\) and \(V_n\) independent, and the Gaussian-cell assumption gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(U_n\mid\mathcal H_{\mathrm{rec},n})
 =\operatorname{Var}(V_n\mid\mathcal H_{\mathrm{rec},n})
 =\frac{\sigma_n^2}{n}\left(1+\frac1n\right).
 \tag{15}
\]
Equations (5), (7), and (8) imply
\[
 G_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}=U_n+c_{n,\ell}V_n
 +g_{n,\ell}^\top E_{W,n}^\top\beta_n,
 \tag{16}
\]
\[
 s_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^2
 =\frac{\sigma_n^2}{n}
 \left[\|g_{n,\ell}\|_2^2+left(1+\frac1n\right)
 (1+c_{n,\ell}^2)\right].
 \tag{17}
\]
Equations (9) and (17), together with the lower noise-scale bound, verify
\(\min_{m,\ell}s_{m,n,\ell}\ge c n^{-1/2}\), completing the deferred variance-floor check for the constructed member.

Let
\[
 Z_*:=\frac{U_n+V_n}{\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(U_n+V_n\mid\mathcal H_{\mathrm{rec},n})}}
 \sim N(0,1).
\]
Uniformly in \(\ell\le H_n\), equations (5), (15), and (17) give
\[
 c_{n,\ell}=1+O(H_n/n),\qquad
 \left|\frac{s_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}}
 {\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(U_n+V_n\mid\mathcal H_{\mathrm{rec},n})}}-1\right|
 =O(H_n/n).
 \tag{18}
\]
The standardized terminal term in (16) has marginal variance \(O(1/n)\).  Its Gaussian union bound and tail integration therefore give expected maximum
\(O(\sqrt{\log(2H_n)/n})\).  Using (18) for the two common terms in (16) yields
\[
 \mathbb E\max_{\ell\le H_n}
 \left|\frac{G_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}}{s_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}}-Z_*\right|
 \le K\left\{\frac{H_n}{n}+
 \sqrt{\frac{\log(2H_n)}n}\right\}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{19}
\]
Since
\[
 \left|\max_{\ell\le H_n}
 \left|\frac{G_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}}{s_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}}\right|-|Z_*|\right|
 \le\max_{\ell\le H_n}
 \left|\frac{G_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}}{s_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}}-Z_*\right|,
\]
(19) proves convergence in mean and probability of the recursive maximum to \(|Z_*|\).  Therefore
\[
 \kappa_{\mathrm{rec},n}\longrightarrow\mathbb E|Z_*|=\sqrt{2/\pi}.
 \tag{20}
\]
The distribution of \(|Z_*|\) is continuous and strictly increasing on \([0,\infty)\); the same probability convergence implies convergence of every fixed interior quantile to its \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile
\(\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\).  Together, (1)--(20) prove every asserted subclass identity and limit.
